issue: Configured 24-bar embargo parameter recorded in metadata but inactive in expanding-window split()
mathematical_and_architectural_rationale: 1. In expanding-window walk-forward validation, training data strictly precedes test data in chronological time. Fold 1 trains on [0, T1_train] and tests on [T1_test, T2_test]. Fold 2 trains on [0, T2_train] and tests on [T2_test, T3_test]. 2. In this sequential design, training observations are strictly in the historical past relative to the current test fold. A post-test embargo (Lopez de Prado, AFML Ch. 7) is mathematically required for K-fold cross-validation where training data occurs chronologically AFTER test data. In expanding walk-forward, post-test training never occurs for the current fold. 3. The 12-bar forward purge between training end and test start (train_end = test_start - 12) strictly prevents training labels from overlapping into the test window. 4. The 12-bar test horizon protection (effective_test_end = test_end - 12) strictly prevents test labels from peeking past the fold boundary. 5. Therefore, inserting an artificial 24-bar embargo hole in historical expanding-window training data is mathematically redundant and creates unnecessary data loss. 6. Formally deprecating the embargo parameter for expanding walk-forward validation maintains 100% integrity without modifying historical fold indices or recalculating existing benchmark metrics.

training_purge.purpose: Prevents training labels from overlapping forward into the test window

test_label_horizon_protection.purpose: Prevents test labels from peeking into future data beyond the test window

post_test_embargo.historical_manifest_action: Preserve historical records with explanatory governance documentation
post_test_embargo.code_action: Update validation documentation and contracts to clarify that expanding walk-forward validation does not require post-test embargoing
